rule: The input is a noise field of one non-zero color (e.g. 8 or 4) on a 0 background. Hidden in the noise is a set of axis-aligned SOLID all-zero rectangular "bars" that form a connected cross / plus / T / comb shape: one or more VERTICAL bars (a contiguous group of fully-zero columns spanning a tall contiguous row-range) plus one or more HORIZONTAL "arm" bars (a contiguous group of fully-zero rows spanning a wide column-range). Each drawn bar is surrounded by a 1-cell all-zero "margin" before the noise begins; consequently the maximal all-zero rectangle for each bar is exactly the bar PLUS a 1-cell border. The transform = recolor the interior of every such bar to color 3 (leaving everything else unchanged), i.e. take each bar's maximal all-zero rectangle and ERODE it by 1 cell on every side that faces noise (NOT on sides that touch the grid boundary, and NOT on sides where the bar merges into a perpendicular bar at a junction — those sides stay so the cross is seamlessly connected). Bars touch the grid edge or connect to a perpendicular bar that does. Output grid = input with all bar-interior cells set to 3.
notes:
DEPLOYED: neurogolf/data/working/task255.onnx is READY=True at 12.205 pts (fat, uses external .onnx.data). To beat it you must produce an EXACT compact build.

RULE (verified by inspection on all 4 train+test): fill rectangular all-zero "bars" with color 3. The bars form a connected cross/plus/T/comb (>=1 vertical bar + >=1 horizontal arm; thicknesses range 1..10; arms branch left and/or right at various rows; test[0] has TWO vertical bars cols10-13 and cols19-21 plus one wide arm rows9-15). Each bar's maximal all-zero rectangle = bar + a 1-cell zero margin; the fill = that rectangle eroded by 1 on noise-facing sides only (NOT grid-edge sides, NOT junction sides).

WHY NOT COMPACT-ONNX-EXPRESSIBLE (tractability=1): exact solution needs (a) connected-component labeling to pick the dominant structure and (b) rectangle decomposition with junction-aware erosion. ONNX rules forbid Loop/Scan/If and CC labeling.

CLOSEST CLEAN RULE I FOUND (does NOT reproduce all; ~mean 14 cell errors, 0/265 exact, but missing=0 i.e. it is always a SUPERSET): fill = largest 4-connected component of ERODE3x3(input==0) with grid-border treated as zero (scipy: binary_erosion(zero, ones((3,3)), border_value=1) then ndimage.label, take max-size comp). Every true-fill cell satisfies ERODE3x3 (confirmed: 0 fill cells lack an all-zero 3x3 nbhd). The only error is EXTRA cells = non-rectangular "bumps" where noise happens to align into a 3x3-clear protrusion off a bar (8-31 extra cells/example).

BEST near-exact numpy (greedy maximal-rectangle peeler, junction-aware erode) in /tmp/solve255b.py: ndiff 3-16 on train+test, 27/261 arc-gen. Algorithm: greedily pop maximal all-zero rects (histogram method) with min(h,w)>=2 & area>=8, mark raw region R; for each bar erode side s by 1 iff (s not at grid edge) AND (the line just beyond s is not fully inside R). Fails because consuming a rect splits the perpendicular bar so arms cannot cross the spine (e.g. train2 arm found cols0-6 but should be cols0-15), and junction seams of 1-2 cells remain.

CONCRETE PLAN TO MAKE IT EXACT (then golf): (1) Detect bars WITHOUT consuming. Find ALL vertical bars: for each maximal run of consecutive columns that are each solid-zero over a common contiguous row-band of height>=~6, that run+band is a vertical bar. Same for horizontal. (2) For each bar, erode by 1 on a side ONLY IF the adjacent line is noise (has a nonzero) AND not a grid edge; leave sides that abut another bar's raw rectangle. (3) Union all eroded bars; junctions merge automatically because a full-width arm and a full-height spine share the crossing rectangle, and you do NOT erode the spine-facing end of the arm (it sees only zeros/other-bar there). Verify on all 265 before building.

ONNX BUILD IDEA IF YOU GET EXACT NUMPY: this is fundamentally region-growth. If the bars are guaranteed border-anchored (they appear to be), an UNROLLED flood-fill is legal ONNX (no Loop): seed = border cells of a 'core' mask, then ~30 iterations of guarded dilation core_t+1 = core_t OR (shift(core_t) AND coremask). Each tensor is 30x30 int8 (tiny, ~900 bytes). BUT the bump problem means flood-fill of the 3x3-eroded mask is a SUPERSET, not exact — you must additionally rectangularize. A working compact path: per-row/per-col projection bars. rule: Template/key replication with per-target scaling. The grid contains exactly ONE "template" blob (the only 8-connected nonzero component that contains color-1 cells) and several "target" blobs (pure color-2 components). The template encodes a relative arrangement of color-2 ANCHOR blocks plus a color-1 DECORATION drawn relative to those anchors, all at unit scale (template anchor edge = kt pixels, usually 1). The target color-2 blocks are solid KxK squares; they appear in groups, each group reproducing the template's anchor arrangement at scale K (number of target blobs is always na*g where na=template anchor count and g=number of groups; observed na in {1,2}, blobs/group multiples 1,2,3). For each matching group of na target blocks, the template's color-1 decoration is stamped scaled by factor K: every unit decoration cell (ur,uc) relative to the anchor-grid origin maps to a KxK block of 1s at pixel (r0+(ur-ur0)*K, c0+(uc-uc0)*K), where (r0,c0) is the group's anchor-origin top-left. The original template (and its 1s) is left unchanged; existing target 2-blocks are preserved; only 1s are added. Some arc-gen groups additionally appear in reflected/rotated orientations of the template arrangement (orientation must be matched per group), and in some cases the entire template motif is replicated at lone single-cell 2-markers.
notes:
VERDICT: NOT compact-ONNX tractable. Do not attempt a real compact build; leave deployed 35484-byte/12.7pt model in place. Reasons: the rule fundamentally requires (1) 8-connected-component labeling to isolate the template blob (the one containing color 1) vs the pure-2 target blobs — forbidden per rules; (2) sub-component labeling of color-2 anchor blocks within each blob; (3) measuring each target block's edge size K (varies per group: 1,2,3,...); (4) grouping target blocks into sets of na (=template anchor count) whose relative top-left arrangement, after dividing by K, equals the template's unit anchor arrangement — combinatorial matching; (5) per-group DYNAMIC SCALING of the color-1 decoration by K (KxK expansion of each unit decoration cell) positioned at the group origin. Standard opset (no Loop/Scan/If, no CC labeling, no data-dependent shapes/scaling) cannot express any of steps 1-5. 

NUMPY REFERENCE STATUS: /tmp/ref101c.py (also /tmp/ref101b.py) reproduces ALL train (3/3) + test (1/1) EXACTLY, confirming the core rule with certainty. On the 262 arc-gen it reaches 174/262; the remaining 88 are the same rule but with target groups appearing in REFLECTED/ROTATED orientations of the template anchor arrangement (my matcher only tests the identity orientation) and a sub-family where the whole template motif is tiled onto lone single-cell 2-markers. To reach 262/262 in numpy: in the grouping loop, when matching a candidate combo of na target blocks against the template's unit anchor set, test all 8 dihedral transforms (4 rotations x 2 reflections) of the template's (uanch, u1) coordinates and apply the matched transform to the decoration before the KxK stamp; and add a fallback that detects isolated single 2-cells and stamps a full scaled copy of the template (anchors+decoration) at each. Distribution confirmed: tmplAnchors=1 -> targetBlobs in {1,2,3}; tmplAnchors=2 -> targetBlobs in {2,4,6} (always a clean multiple => g groups).

rule: Each grid contains ONE "template" shape and one-or-more "seed" shapes (1-3 seeds). A seed = two equal-size, adjacent, solid rectangular blocks of different colors filling their joint bounding box (a "marker" block + a "body" block). The template = the remaining shape: a single marker cell (color M, the minority color appears exactly once) surrounded by body cells in a fixed arrangement. Build the template's OFFSET MASK = set of (dr,dc) offsets (in unit/block coordinates) of each body cell relative to the single marker cell. Transformation: leave the template untouched; for every seed, keep its marker block in place and STAMP the body block (filled with the seed's body color) at every template offset, where each offset (dr,dc) maps to a block-sized translation: top-left = marker_top_left + (dr*blockH, dc*blockW). The marker color M is shared across all shapes in a grid; for each seed the marker color = M, body = the other color, blockH/blockW = the seed marker-block height/width. IMPORTANT: the template orientation is applied AS-IS (no rotation per seed) — the seed's own marker->body direction does NOT re-orient the mask. Offsets/blocks outside the grid are clipped.
notes:
VERIFIED RULE (numpy reference reproduces ALL 5 train+test AND all 262 arc-gen exactly, see below). FAMILY = connected-component; INTRACTABLE in allowed opset. Do NOT spend build budget — keep the deployed fat model (neurogolf/data/working/task133.onnx, 24395B, 12.84pts).

WHY INTRACTABLE: the rule requires (a) connected-component labeling to isolate each shape, (b) per-shape classification template-vs-seed, (c) per-shape bbox + block-size measurement, (d) per-shape minority-color (marker) detection. Critically, 136/267 grids contain MULTIPLE seeds with DIFFERENT block sizes (block dims range 1..8) in the SAME grid, and the template offset mask must be scaled by EACH seed's own block size. A fixed conv kernel cannot adapt scale per-shape, and CC labeling needs Loop/Scan/If which are banned. No CC-free / pure-morphology formulation exists.

EXACT NUMPY REFERENCE (drop-in, passes 267/267):
```python
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage
def solve(inp):
    inp=np.array(inp); H,W=inp.shape; out=inp.copy()
    lab,n=ndimage.label(inp>0)
    comps=[]
    for c in range(1,n+1):
        ys,xs=np.where(lab==c); comps.append((ys.min(),ys.max(),xs.min(),xs.max(),ys,xs))
    template=None; seeds=[]
    for (y0,y1,x0,x1,ys,xs) in comps:
        sub=inp[y0:y1+1,x0:x1+1]; cols=sorted(set(inp[ys,xs].tolist()))
        seed=False
        if len(cols)==2 and (sub!=0).all():
            cnt={k:int((sub==k).sum()) for k in cols}
            if cnt[cols[0]]==cnt[cols[1]]:
                def rect(k):
                    m=(sub==k);yy,xx=np.where(m);return m[yy.min():yy.max()+1,xx.min():xx.max()+1].all()
                if rect(cols[0]) and rect(cols[1]): seed=True
        (seeds if seed else [None]).append((y0,y1,x0,x1,sub)) if seed else None
        if not seed: template=(y0,y1,x0,x1,sub)
    if template is None: return out
    _,_,_,_,tsub=template
    tcols=sorted(set(tsub[tsub!=0].tolist())); cnt={k:int((tsub==k).sum()) for k in tcols}
    M=min(cnt,key=lambda k:cnt[k]); mr,mc=[v[0] for v in np.where(tsub==M)]
    tmask=[(r-mr,cc-mc) for r in range(tsub.shape[0]) for cc in range(tsub.shape[1]) if tsub[r,cc]!=0 and tsub[r,cc]!=M]
    for (y0,y1,x0,x1,sub) in seeds:
        cols=sorted(set(sub[sub!=0].tolist()))
        mk=M if M in cols else cols[0]; bd=[k for k in cols if k!=mk][0]
        myy,mxx=np.where(sub==mk)
        bh=myy.max()-myy.min()+1; bw=mxx.max()-mxx.min()+1
        mtop=y0+myy.min(); mleft=x0+mxx.min()
        for (dr,dc) in tmask:
            rr=mtop+dr*bh; cc=mleft+dc*bw
            for i in range(bh):
                for j in range(bw):
                    r2,c2=rr+i,cc+j
                    if 0<=r2<H and 0<=c2<W: out[r2,c2]=bd
        out[mtop:mtop+bh,mleft:mleft+bw]=mk
    return out
```
(Note: in the reference above the seed-append line is awkward; cleaner: if seed: seeds.append(...) else: template=... . The tested version used that clean branch and scored 267/267.)

rule: Each input is a set of scattered "objects". An object = one multi-cell main shape (color C = the most frequent color in that 8-connected component) plus up to 3 single "seed" cells clustered at ONE corner of the shape's bounding box (the two edge-adjacent cells and the one diagonal cell of that outside corner). Each seed has its own color S (sometimes S equals C for the diagonal seed). The output keeps the original shape and every seed cell, and for EACH seed it draws a recolored, reflected copy of the main shape placed adjacent on the seed's side: seed to the LEFT/RIGHT -> shape mirrored left-right, placed flush on that side; seed ABOVE/BELOW -> shape mirrored up-down, placed flush; seed at a DIAGONAL corner -> shape rotated 180 (both-axis mirror), placed flush diagonally. Placement: the reflected copy occupies a bounding box of the same size as the shape, abutting the original shape's bbox on the seed's side (tr = r0-sh / r1+1 / r0, tc = c0-sw / c1+1 / c0 with the LR/UD flips). Verified exactly by hand on 4 separate objects across train0/train1/train2/test (color7 shape with 3 seeds -> UD-above, 180-up-right, LR-right copies all reproduced cell-for-cell; color3 shape -> LR-left + 180-up-left; color2 shape -> LR/UD/180 triple).
notes:
DO NOT attempt a compact ONNX for task285 - it is genuinely NOT ONNX-expressible under the standard-opset / no-Loop/Scan/If / no-connected-component constraints. Reasons: (1) Objects are scattered across the grid and each shape must be reflected INDEPENDENTLY of the others, which requires connected-component labeling to group each shape with its seeds. (2) Shapes vary in size (4-9 cells, often with diagonal-only internal links and diagonal protrusions), so each reflection uses a per-object variable bounding box - no fixed-window conv/morphology can do it. (3) A seed can share the shape's main color (the diagonal corner seed), so separating shape vs seed requires CC analysis, not a global color/threshold op. (4) The copy placement is anchored to each object's own bbox corner (tr=r0-sh|r1+1|r0, tc=c0-sw|c1+1|c0), again per-object. The deployed model (neurogolf/data/working/task285.onnx, ~65829 bytes, thousands of nodes) is CORRECT and verifies READY=True points=13.274 - keep it; do not replace with a lookup table (would score 0 on hidden test and is forbidden).

rule: The input contains one large solid rectangle of color-2 ("the canvas", which becomes the output grid) plus several small 3x3 "key" tiles scattered in the 0-background outside the canvas. Each key tile is a 2-background 3x3 with exactly one foreground color C marking a small shape (e.g. `223/222/223` = color 3 at two corners). Inside the canvas there are several "marker" regions made of 0-holes; each marker is a (D4-rotated/reflected) copy of one key's pattern. The transformation: (1) crop to the canvas; (2) turn every hole back into 2; (3) for each hole-marker, identify which key it corresponds to by matching the marker's 0-pattern against the key's pattern under the 8 dihedral (D4) symmetries, and stamp that key's foreground color C onto the canvas at the marker's location, in the matching orientation. The output is the canvas (all 2s) with each matched key's colored foreground stamped where its marker sat. Net effect: each "stencil" of 0-holes in the canvas is replaced by the corresponding key's colored glyph. NOTE: the exact foreground/background-to-hole alignment convention has subtle cases (when a key's pattern is partially symmetric or sits at a canvas edge, the same hole-window can match multiple key orientations / two keys can share a bg-mask) and a global non-overlap/bijection disambiguation is needed; the simple "hole-mask == key background-mask, stamp foreground" model reproduces the test case and ~84% of arc-gen but not the full alignment for the remaining ~15%.
notes:
DO NOT attempt a compact ONNX build for task233 — it is NOT expressible as branch-free standard ONNX. The rule requires: (a) localizing a VARIABLE-position, variable-size solid-2 rectangle (the "canvas") whose bbox = output shape; (b) connected-component grouping of 0-hole "marker" regions inside the canvas (markers are often NOT 4- or 8-connected — e.g. arc-gen[1] has a plus-marker split into two pieces, so true grouping is "which 3x3 window of holes belongs together", a combinatorial tiling, not a CC pass); (c) extracting a dictionary of 3x3 "key" tiles (2-background + one foreground color) from the 0-background OUTSIDE the canvas; (d) matching each marker to a key under the 8 D4 symmetries; (e) stamping the key's foreground color in the matched orientation; plus (f) GLOBAL disambiguation when a marker's hole-mask matches multiple key orientations or two keys share a background mask. All of (a)-(f) need data-dependent loops / connected components / argmax-over-dictionary placement — none expressible without Loop/Scan/If or CC labeling. Tractability=1.

rule: Object-relocation / template-stamping with anisotropic affine warp. (1) Determine the FILLER color = the most frequent non-zero color. (2) Find all 8-connected components of non-zero cells. The TEMPLATE is the component containing the most filler cells: a small 2D "creature" with one filler-colored body and exactly three distinct MARKER cells (the three non-filler, non-zero colors — e.g. {1,2,4} or {1,3,4}), one marker of each color embedded in/at the ends of the body. (3) Every OTHER component that also contains filler is a DECOY and is deleted (does not appear in output). (4) The remaining non-zero cells are isolated single MARKER pixels scattered around the grid. Group them into TARGET triangles by nearest-neighbor matching: each target has exactly one pixel of each of the three marker colors, and the marker pixels stay EXACTLY where they are in the input (they are not moved). (5) For each target triangle, compute the unique 2x2 linear map M that sends the template's two marker offset-vectors (marker_origin->marker_A, marker_origin->marker_B) onto the target's corresponding two offset-vectors. M is a general (possibly anisotropic, reflecting, shearing) linear transform, NOT restricted to the 8 rigid dihedral orientations. (6) Apply M to every template body cell (taking the lowest marker color as the origin), round to grid, and paint the filler/markers into the output, so the template body is re-drawn stretched to connect the three already-placed target markers. (7) The original template component is removed (it only seeds the shape, the body is re-stamped at the targets). Net effect: scattered marker triangles get the warped creature drawn onto them; all filler-bearing source objects (template + decoys) disappear from their original positions.
notes:
RULE IS INTRACTABLE FOR COMPACT GENUINE ONNX — recommend leaving the deployed genuine 13.371pt model in place; do not deploy a lookup table.

WHY INTRACTABLE (allowed opset has no Loop/Scan/If, no connected-component labeling):
1. Requires connected-component labeling THREE ways: (a) find the max-filler template component, (b) identify & delete every other filler-bearing decoy component, (c) group the scattered isolated marker singletons into target triangles by nearest-neighbor color matching. CC labeling is explicitly not expressible.
2. Variable number of target instances per grid (2-4 in the examples) — would need a Loop.
3. Per-instance ANISOTROPIC affine warp (M = C @ inv(T), a full 2x2 with scaling/shear/reflection that differs per target) followed by grid rasterization of the template body. Even with a fixed instance budget, the per-instance variable-scale warp + line-fill rasterization is very hard to express with fixed-topology ops.

rule: Cross/plus template completion. The grid contains small "cross" shapes, each = a center cell of color C surrounded by arm cells of color A, in one of 4 geometries: (a) horizontal line A-C-A (1x3), (b) vertical line A/C/A (3x1), (c) orthogonal plus (.A./A C A/.A. with arms at the 4 orthogonal distance-1 neighbors), (d) diagonal X (A.A/.C./A.A with arms at the 4 diagonal neighbors). At least one COMPLETE cross of each active color-pair always exists in the input, which establishes the binding (A,C) and the geometry for that center color. Throughout the grid there are PARTIAL copies of these crosses: loose single center-dots (color C, arms missing), arm-only rings (all arm cells present, center missing), and arm-pairs (the two arms of a 1D ACA present, center missing). The transformation COMPLETES every partial copy into the full cross: loose center-dot C -> stamp arms A in its geometry around it; ring/arm-pair -> fill the missing center with C. Existing nonzero cells never change color; only background cells are filled. The arm<->center binding is data-dependent and globally unique per input (arm-color set and center-color set are disjoint; 71 distinct ordered (arm,center) pairs across the corpus), so a fixed convolution cannot solve it — the binding must be recovered at runtime via a global per-color reduction (e.g. arm color of center c = dominant nonzero neighbor of c-cells, or co-occurrence MatMul).

rule: Each input has a solid background (most common border color), one solid axis-aligned rectangle (the unique non-bg color with >=40 cells, call it F), one or more single-pixel "seed" markers (color M) sitting inside rectangle(s), and one free-floating 5x5-ish "legend" cross drawn on the background. The legend is a plus/cross: center color = M; its 4 arms carry a "line" color (vertical arm color Lv, horizontal arm color Lh) and its diagonal-adjacent cells may carry a "corner" color K. An arm that reaches distance 2 from center marks that axis as "extending". Transformation: (1) erase the legend (set its cells to bg). (2) For every seed of color M inside a rectangle, stamp the legend's exact local pattern (its 5x5 neighborhood, bg cells transparent) centered on the seed, clipped to the rectangle. (3) If the legend's vertical arm extends (length 2), draw a full vertical line of color Lv through the seed, clipped to the contiguous F-run of its rectangle column; likewise a full horizontal line of color Lh if the horizontal arm extends. The seed center and the K corners come from the stamp; the long arms become the full lines. Detection: legend center = bbox-center of the connected non-bg/non-F pixels that have no F within Chebyshev distance 2 (legend floats on bg; seeds are surrounded by F). Legend center coords are always in [3,26] so a 5x5 patch around it is always in-bounds.

KEY MEMORY TRICK that won (drove mem from 1.06MB -> 26KB): do ALL legend/template/color sampling on a TINY [1,1,5,5] patch dynamically Sliced from g at (cy-2,cx-2), NOT by shifting full-grid masks. cy,cx are floats from bbox-center reductions; Cast->int64, build start=[cy-2,cx-2] end=[cy+3,cx+3], Slice axes [2,3]. Patch present-mask = (patch!=bg); value-kernel pval = patch*present; M = patch cell (2,2); arm colors/ext flags = static Slices of patch cells (1,2)(3,2)(2,1)(2,3) and (0,2)(4,2)(2,0)(2,4).

PIPELINE (all numpy-verified in /tmp/onnxsim3.py, exact 266/266):
1. g = sum_c c*onehot(input)  [Mul colors + ReduceSum ch].
2. bg = ArgMax of per-color BORDER counts (input*bmask, ReduceSum). F = ArgMax of total per-color counts with bg channel penalized by -1e4.
3. nonbgF = 1-isbg-isF. Fd = MaxPool(isF,5x5,pad2). cc = nonbgF*(Fd<=0).
4. center: xmin/ymin = ReduceMin over (cc?ix:1e4); xmax/ymax = ReduceMax over (cc?ix:-1e4); cx=floor((xmin+xmax)/2), cy likewise.
5. patch extraction (the win, above). Lv = pU?vU:vD ; Lh = pL?vL:vR ; vert_ext=clip(pU2+pD2,0,1); horiz_ext=clip(pL2+pR2,0,1).
6. legend mask = (|ix-cx|<=2 & |iy-cy|<=2) * nonbgF. seed = (g==M)*(1-legend). run = max(isF, seed).
7. LINE CLIPPING without connected-components or WxW broadcast (critical for memory): run_has_seed via cumulative ops only, all [1,1,30,30]. seg_left(seed,run,axis): cs=CumSum(seed,axis); base=cummax(cs*(1-run),axis); sl=cs-base. Mirror with reversed seed/run (Slice step -1) to get sr. total=sl+sr-seed; hit=(total>0)*run. cummax implemented by log-doubling: 5 iterations of Max(cur, shift_right(cur,2^k)) where shift = Pad(value -1e9)+Slice. Hh=run_has_seed(...,axis3)*horiz_ext, Vv=...*vert_ext.
8. compose color grid: o0=g*(1-legend)+bg*legend; o1=o0*(1-Hh)+Lh*Hh; o2=o1*(1-Vv)+Lv*Vv. inside=max(isF,seed,Hh,Vv).
9. STAMP via Conv (collapses a 25-iter loop to 2 ops; verified non-conflicting on all 266 in /tmp/convstamp.py even though min seed chebyshev sep is 4): Vk=flip(pval), Pk=flip(ppres) [Slice step -1 on axes 2,3]; stampval=Conv(seed,Vk,pad2); stamppres=Conv(seed,Pk,pad2); apply=(stamppres>0.5)*inside; finalg=o2*(1-apply)+stampval*apply.
10. OUTPUT (avoid a 144KB float [1,10,30,30] intermediate): active=Greater(ReduceSum(input,ch),0.5); fgm=finalg*active+(active-1)*1e4 (out-of-grid -> -1e4 so it matches no color); oh_b=Equal(fgm,colors) [single [1,10,30,30] bool, ~9KB]; Cast(oh_b)->'output' (the tensor named 'output' is FREE per scorer).

Remaining 26KB is ~5 full-grid float32 tensors in the line/compose chains + the 9KB output bool. Could shave more by casting line/compose masks to int8 (Mul/Add/Max/CumSum work on int), but not needed: already +1.23 over deployed. No Loop/Scan/If/NonZero/Unique/Compress used; opset 18 domain "".

rule: A "master" glyph is the color whose densest 3x3 window is largest (equivalently: most cells, ties broken toward the single connected glyph). The master 3x3 pattern is kept unchanged. Every OTHER nonzero color appears as a partial fragment (or single cell) of the SAME 3x3 glyph, located one period-4 step away from the master in exactly one of 8 directions. For each such marker, the output repeats the master glyph — recolored to the marker's color — along that direction at period 4 (3-cell glyph + 1-cell gap), for k=1,2,3,... copies, each copy clipped at the grid border. Direction for a marker = sign of (marker-glyph-position minus master-position) per axis; a marker fragment overlaps the k=1 copy of its direction. The ONNX detects this without connected components: for each color c and each of 8 unit directions d, color c is active in direction d iff (grid==c) overlaps translate(master_mask, 4*d). Then it paints translate(master_mask, 4*k*d) with color c for all k. Background channel = in-grid-extent minus any colored cell.

Build script: neurogolf_claude/rescue/make_task005_compact.py (also /tmp/make005_v3.py). Numpy ref: /tmp/ref005.py (uses scipy.ndimage.label for the reference only; reproduces all 266 exactly).

KEY SCORING INSIGHT (verified by reading neurogolf_utils.calculate_memory): the 'input' and 'output' graph tensors are EXCLUDED from the memory sum (`if tensor_name in ['input','output']: continue`). Memory = sum over every OTHER intermediate tensor of num_elements*dtype_itemsize, taking max size across runs. params = total initializer element count. points = max(1, 25 - ln(memory+params)). So make output int8 (free), use fp16 everywhere (Conv/MatMul/Gemm/AveragePool all support fp16 in ORT; int8 NOT supported by Conv/MatMul/ReduceSum), and crop the working extent to 21x21 (the true max grid; all 266 examples are 21x21) and Pad to 30x30 only at the very end.

ALGORITHM (compact, ~25 nodes, opset 14, the proven make_task005.py ray-stamp idea but golfed):
1. in8 = Cast(input,int8)  [1,10,30,30]=9000 (half of fp16; one-hot is exact in int8).
2. x19i = Slice(in8, ch1..9, 0:21,0:21) int8; x19 = Cast(x19i,fp16) [1,9,21,21].
3. extent gridS = bg0 + occ where bg0=Cast(Slice(in8,ch0,0:21,0:21),fp16), occ=ReduceSum(x19,axis1).
4. master selector tsel: box=AveragePool3x3(x19) [1,9,19,19]; wscore=ReduceMax(box,[2,3]); wmax=ReduceMax(wscore,1); tsel=Sign(wscore-wmax)+1  (1 at master channel else 0). NOTE AveragePool/box is the densest-window detector and is REQUIRED for tie cases (e.g. two colors with equal cell counts); simple argmax-of-cell-count fails. Verified box matches true master on all 266.
5. kflat=Reshape(x19,[9,441]); tmpl(master plane [1,1,21,21]) = Reshape(MatMul(Reshape(tsel,[1,9]), kflat),[1,1,21,21]) — this MatMul trick AVOIDS materializing a [1,9,21,21] xt tensor (saved ~8000 bytes).
6. tsum = Conv(tmpl, wall, pads=4*KMAX) [1,8,21,21]: wall is [8,1,(2*4*KMAX+1)^2] with ones at offsets 4*j*dir for j=1..KMAX, per direction d. KMAX=4 used (kernel 33x33, 8745 params). Observed MAX copies across ALL 266 examples = 3, so KMAX=3 (25x25 kernel, 5039 params) ALSO passes all and scores 13.600 — chose KMAX=4 for a one-copy safety margin against hidden edge cases (still 13.560). The generator never exceeds 3.
7. tsumflat=Reshape(tsum,[8,441]). ov=Gemm(kflat, tsumflat, transB=1) [9,8] (Gemm transB avoids an explicit Transpose tensor). act=Sign(ov). Using tsum (all copies) for detection instead of a separate s1 single-shift Conv is SAFE and saves ~14000 bytes: a marker fragment at master+4*dirA can only coincide with tsum's dirB k-th copy if dirA==dirB,k==1, so no false activations.
8. stamp=MatMul(act, tsumflat) [9,441] fp16. stamp8=Cast(stamp,int8); sp8=Reshape(stamp8,[1,9,21,21]) — cast-then-reshape in int8 (cheaper than fp16 reshape).
9. master glyph in output: tsel8=Cast(tsel,int8); xt8=Mul(x19i,tsel8) int8 (int8 Mul needs opset>=14). c19=Max(sp8,xt8).
10. background: gridSi=Cast(gridS,int8); coloredSi=ReduceMax(c19,1); bgSi=Sub(gridSi,coloredSi) (int8 Sub, opset>=14) -> 1 only in-grid&uncolored, <=0 elsewhere (verifier does result>0 so negatives drop).
11. y10i=Concat([bgSi,c19],axis1) [1,10,21,21] int8; output=Pad(y10i,[0,0,0,0, 0,0,9,9]).

GOTCHAS: opset 14 (int8 Mul/Add/Sub need >=14; ReduceSum needs axes-as-INPUT in opset>=13 -> use an 'axes1' int64 initializer; ReduceMax keeps axes attribute until opset 18). Output MUST be int8 not bool (Pad rejects bool). Conv/MatMul/AveragePool reject int8 -> keep those in fp16. The verifier crashes its debug display on a malformed/oversized predicted grid, so debug with raw onnxruntime and compare (result>0) vs one-hot, not the verifier, until correct.

FURTHER COMPACTION IDEAS (to push beyond 13.56, none yet realized): the remaining big counted tensors are in8(9000), x19/stamp/kflat fp16 (7938 each), tsum/tsumflat (7056 each), box(6498). box is the AveragePool master detector — strided pooling breaks detection (6-17 mismatches), so it seems irreducible without a cheaper correct detector. A correct sub-7938 master detector or eliminating one of the redundant fp16 [9,441] reshapes would gain ~0.05-0.1 more points.

rule: Each grid uses color 0 (background), color 2 (markers), and exactly ONE other nonzero "shape color". The shape-color cells and 2-cells are arranged so that, together, they form SOLID rectangular blocks (every cell inside the block's bounding box is either a 2 or the shape color, with NO zeros inside; every block is >=2 in both height and width, observed heights 2-3, widths 2-7). Transformation: for every such solid rectangle that contains at least one 2, recolor that rectangle's SHAPE-COLOR cells to 4. The 2-cells stay 2; all cells not inside such a rectangle are unchanged. Equivalently: a shape-color cell becomes 4 iff it belongs to the stamped solid {2,shape} rectangle object that holds a marker. (Color-canonicalizing to 0/shape=1/two=2, the 4-label is a deterministic function of a 5x5 window with ZERO contradictions over all 266 cases, but the separating function is effectively global rectangle/object identity, not a simple local geometric predicate.)
notes:
RULE is solid: "fill shape-color cells of every solid {2,shape}-rectangle that contains a 2 with color 4". Best numpy reference reaches 264/266 (ALL train+test pass; only arc-gen[53] and arc-gen[243] fail). Reference saved at /Users/kanxiao/IdeaProjects/kaggletest/neurogolf_claude/scratch/ref_task077.py (iterative min-AREA bbox-merge of 2-cells: seed each 2 as a 1x1 box, repeatedly merge the pair whose union bbox stays all-{2,shape} and has the SMALLEST resulting area, to fixpoint; then fill shape cells inside every final box). The 2 failures are genuine generator ambiguities where two distinct stamped rectangles are bridged by an incidental solid {2,shape} corridor, and greedy geometry merges/splits them differently than the generator did.

WHY NOT ONNX-TRACTABLE (tractability=1): The correct algorithm is connected-component / object-detection class. Identifying which 2s share a rectangle requires iterative region merging (fixpoint loop) -> needs Loop/Scan or data-dependent control flow, which the verifier forbids. There is NO bounded fixed-op formulation that is both correct and generalizing:
  - "shape cell 8-adjacent to a 2": FN=0 but huge FP (catches every shape cell next to any 2). 211/266 if you instead use bbox-of-8-connected-2-blobs, but fails when one rectangle's 2s are not 8-connected (separated by shape cells), e.g. train0 bottom 3x5 block.
  - "shape cell inside ANY fully-blk 2x2 containing a 2": FN=0 but FP=15376 (incidental solid noise patches qualify). Only 3/266.
  - "shape cell inside a maximal solid {2,shape} rectangle (h>=2,w>=2) containing a 2": overshoots because true rectangles are NOT maximal (they can grow into adjacent shape-only solid patches) -> ~30 diffs on train0.
  - Local 5x5 rect-search rule: 1/266 (too permissive). The 5x5 zero-contradiction result is a property of the data distribution, NOT evidence of a compact local geometric rule; the true function is essentially a lookup over object identity.

RECOMMENDATION: Do NOT attempt a compact ONNX. Any build that hits 266 would be a memorized lookup table (forbidden; won't generalize to hidden test). The deployed fat-but-correct model (/Users/kanxiao/IdeaProjects/kaggletest/neurogolf/data/working/task077.onnx + .onnx.data, ~26KB, 13.51 pts) should be LEFT IN PLACE. If a future ONNX opset (or the verifier) ever permits Loop/iterative ops, the 264/266 reference is the algorithm to port; the remaining 2 arc-gen cases need the generator's true object-split which is not recoverable from final-grid geometry alone. No winner saved to rescue/.

rule: The grid contains exactly one multi-color "key" shape (cells of colors 1-7 or 9) and several solid color-8 blobs. Every 8-blob is an exact translate of the key's occupied-cell mask. Transformation: stamp the key's full color pattern onto each 8-blob (aligning the key's bounding-box top-left to the blob's bounding-box top-left), then delete the original key and all bare 8s. All other cells become background (color 0). Output grid has the same H x W extent as the input. Verified: every one of the 264 train+test+arc-gen examples has exactly one key blob and all 8-blobs match the key mask, so no connected-component analysis is needed — anchor detection by sliding correlation suffices.

WINNER SHIPPED: /Users/kanxiao/IdeaProjects/kaggletest/neurogolf_claude/rescue/task069.onnx — READY=True, 14.754 pts (baseline was 13.84), 1853 bytes, 28112 mem + 51 params. It uses cropkit.const but a custom _finalize_bool_output (declares output as BOOL).

ALGORITHM (fully static, no connected components, single color channel):
 0) Two 1x1 Convs on fp32 `input`: keyc32 = sum over channels {1..7,9} weighted by color index (channel c -> value c; ch0,ch8 -> 0) => integer key-color grid; eight32 = select channel 8 => 0/1 mask. active32 = ReduceMax(input, axis=1) => in-grid extent (1 where any channel set, since one-hot partitions). Cast all three [1,1,30,30] results to FLOAT16 (keyc, eight, active) so the whole downstream pipeline is half-width. Do NOT cast the 10-channel input to fp16 — that creates an 18000-byte tensor and loses the win; cast only the three 1-channel reductions.
 1) keep_row[1,1,30,1]/keep_col[1,1,1,30] = (ReduceMax(keyc over col/row) > 0). Threshold on the 1-D reductions to avoid a 30x30 iskey map.
 2) Small direct gather of the key's top-left KHxKW (KH=3,KW=4, the max key bbox over all examples) WITHOUT a 30x30 compaction: build Sr3[1,1,3,30] = (iota_kh == cumsum(keep_row)-1) * keep_row, and Tc4[1,1,30,4] = (cumsum(keep_col)-1 == iota_kw) * keep_col; then Kc = Sr3 @ keyc @ Tc4 => [1,1,3,4] canonical color kernel. (Valid because no key bbox has an empty interior row/col, so gather == translation.) M = (Kc>0) mask kernel; area = sum(M).
 3) Anchor detection: corr = Conv(eight, M, pads=[0,0,KH-1,KW-1]) => [1,1,30,30]; anchor = (corr == area). KEY INSIGHT: corr==area ALONE is a sufficient and correct anchor test (do NOT also require window-8-count==area — that fixed-3x4 extra check actually breaks 16 arc-gen cases where a neighbor blob sits inside the padded window). It works because the 8-cells are a disjoint union of separated key-mask translates.
 4) Stamp: outcolor = ConvTranspose(anchor[fp16], Kc[fp16], pads=[0,0,KH-1,KW-1]) — the pads attribute crops the natural [1,1,32,33] output straight to [1,1,30,30] (the dropped rows/cols are always zero since anchors are in-grid). ConvTranspose with a DYNAMIC (data-derived, non-initializer) weight input is accepted by onnxruntime — confirmed.
 5) Output: outcolor_m = outcolor + (active - 1) (in-grid cells unchanged, out-of-grid -> -1 sentinel). output = Equal(outcolor_m, colors[1,10,1,1]=[0..9]) => one-hot [1,10,30,30] BOOL written DIRECTLY as `output`. Declaring `output` as BOOL is legal: the verifier only does (result>0).astype(float), and calculate_memory skips the tensor named `output`. This removes the 10-channel float Cast (9000-byte bool intermediate eliminated too).

WHY THESE TRICKS MATTER FOR SCORING: memory = sum over EVERY intermediate tensor of num_elements*itemsize; `input` and `output` are excluded. So: (a) work in 1 color channel not 10 one-hot channels — only the excluded output is 10-channel; (b) make `output` the bool Equal result directly; (c) fp16 halves the [1,1,30,30] maps to 1800 bytes; (d) ConvTranspose pads-crop avoids a 4224 stamp_big + Slice; (e) small Sr3/Tc4 gather avoids 7 30x30 compaction maps.

REMAINING FLOOR / IDEAS IF YOU WANT MORE: the three fp32 reads (keyc32, eight32, active32 = 10800 bytes) are the largest remaining cost and are unavoidable while reading the fp32 input (Conv/ReduceMax output dtype follows fp32 input; casting the 10-ch input to fp16 costs 18000 and is worse). Merging them into one multi-output Conv does not help (profiler counts per-tensor element totals, and the extra Split/Slice maps cost more). Could not find a sub-10800 way to read the grid extent + key colors + eight mask. Current 14.754 is a strong local optimum; further gains would need eliminating one of those three fp32 reads entirely.

rule: CRACKED by Claude. Each 23x23 input contains exactly ONE 'key': a 5x5 block whose border+body is color 1 with a constellation of color-4 cells inside (the only region with any 1s). Extract the key's 4-cell constellation K (set of (dr,dc) offsets within the 5x5). Elsewhere the grid has scattered single 4s (noise) PLUS some isolated 5x5 windows containing a 4-constellation that equals a D4 transform (one of 8 rotations/reflections) of K, with all other cells 0. For each such matched window, STAMP: fill the window's 0-cells with 1, keep the 4s (i.e. draw the same 1-frame the key has, in the matching orientation). Lone single 4s are NOT framed. Verified on train0: key 4-set {(1,1),(2,3),(3,1)}; framed region at rows12-16 cols10-14 had 4-set {(1,1),(1,3),(3,2)} = key rotated 90deg.
notes_for_codex: Currently DEPLOYED model is flaky (222/262, scores 0 real). Build plan: (1) Find key = 5x5 bbox of the 1-cells (ReduceMax over color-1 channel along rows/cols, then argmax extents). (2) Extract K = 4-channel values inside that bbox -> 5x5 binary. (3) Precompute its 8 D4 orientations (static perms/flips of a 5x5 = cheap Gather/Transpose). (4) For each orientation g, correlate g(K) against the 4-channel via Conv (kernel=g(K) as 5x5, weight where K=1 -> +1, where K=0 (inside 5x5) -> large negative to forbid stray 4s; matches where conv == popcount(K)). Also require the window has NO 1s already and 4-count in window == |K|. (5) Where matched, scatter the 1-frame: out_1 = max(in_1, dilate5x5(match_centers) AND not 4-cell); keep 4s. All ops are Conv/ReduceMax/Equal/Where/MaxPool-dilation, NO connected-components, NO Loop -> fully legal ONNX, moderate size (~score 12-15). The flaky existing model likely mishandles overlapping matches or the key-vs-match disambiguation. This is the single biggest available single-task win (currently 0 -> ~13).
